integridad.intro: Each record stores a horizontal check digit (DVH) computed from its fields, and each collection stores a vertical one (DVV): the sum of its DVHs. If someone changes, adds or deletes data outside the app, they stop matching.

integridad.confirmarTexto: The current data becomes the valid baseline, including records now flagged as altered. Only do this after reviewing what changed, or after a migration or a restore.

bitacora.intro: Every request to the app and every important event (plan generated, check-in, user deleted) is recorded. Passwords and emails are never stored: the email is shown from the account. Records older than {{dias}} days are deleted automatically.

backup.intro: Saves a copy of every collection on the server (backups/backup_DATE, one file per collection). The last {{retencion}} are kept: creating a new one deletes the oldest.
backup.errorGenerar: Couldn't create the backup. Try again.

backup.restoreTexto: Restoring replaces the current content of each collection with the backup's, so it isn't done from the web: it runs on the server and asks for confirmation. When it finishes it recalculates the check digits.
backup.restoreAyuda: Without a name it restores the latest backup. With --si it doesn't ask (for automation).

ayuda.intro: Short answers to the most common questions about your plan, your progress and your account.

r: When you finish the 4 onboarding steps, FitPocket sends your data (weight, height, age, goal, level, available days and minutes, diet type, budget, limitations and notes) to an artificial intelligence model, which builds a routine and a 7-day diet.

The routine only uses the days you picked. If you marked a limitation (for example knee or lower back), besides asking the AI, the app checks the routine and removes or replaces contraindicated exercises.
It takes from a few seconds to a couple of minutes. The plan is written in the language you had selected when it was generated.

preguntas.p: How do I swap an exercise I can't or don't want to do?
r: In "View my plan", tap the exercise to open it. If the AI suggested alternatives, a "Swap exercise" button appears: each tap shows the next option and goes back to the original after the last one.
The swap only lasts while you're looking at the plan: it isn't saved, and the original exercise shows up again next time.

preguntas.p: How does the daily checklist work?
r: Each day you mark how your routine and your diet went: Done (1 point), Partly (half a point) or Skipped (0). Then tap Save day.
It's recorded once per day: after saving it stays fixed until the next day. Your adherence and streak are calculated from it.

preguntas.p: What is adherence and how is it calculated?
r: It's how much of your plan you followed in the last 7 days, as a percentage.

The diet adds points every day; the routine only on days your plan has a workout (if the plan says rest, you don't lose points for resting). The percentage is what you scored over the maximum possible. Days before your first plan don't count.
If it drops below 50% with at least 3 days counted, the dashboard warns you.
The number of consecutive days, counting back from today, in which you saved the checklist and scored at least some points.
It counts from today: if you haven't saved today yet, it shows 0 until you do. A day without a check-in, or with everything on "Skipped", breaks it.
Body mass index: your weight in kilograms divided by your height in meters squared. It's calculated from the data you entered during onboarding.

As a general reference: under 18.5 is underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 is normal, 25 to 29.9 overweight and 30 or more obesity. It's only a guide: it doesn't tell muscle from fat and doesn't replace a professional's opinion.

preguntas.p: I forgot my password. How do I recover it?
r: Tap "Sign in" and then "Forgot your password?". Enter your account email and you'll get a link to choose a new one.
The link expires in 30 minutes and works only once. Changing it signs you out on other devices. If it doesn't arrive, check your spam folder.

preguntas.p: Which of my data is stored encrypted?
r: Your name, your physical limitations and the note you wrote during onboarding are stored encrypted (AES-256): they can't be read in the database without the server's key.
Your password is never stored: only a hash (bcrypt) that can check it but can't recover it. For the recovery link, only a hash is stored too.
The activity log doesn't store passwords or emails, and every record has a check digit that reveals if someone changes it outside the app.

preguntas.p: How do I delete my account?
r: On the dashboard, open the Progress tab and scroll to "Your account": that's where "Delete my account" is. It asks for confirmation before deleting anything.
Your account, all your plans and all your checklist records are deleted. It can't be undone.

preguntas.p: How do I change the language?
r: With the ES / EN buttons: they are at the top right and, on a phone, some screens show them at the bottom right. The app switches instantly and remembers your choice.
Your plan stays in the language it was generated in.
A permission allows one specific action (for example usuarios.borrar). A family groups permissions and other families too: Administrador includes Usuario.
What someone can do is the sum of their families and individual permissions. Changes apply immediately, without the person signing in again. You can't change your own permissions.

preguntas.p: What do I do if the integrity check flags altered data?
r: It means those records were changed, added or deleted outside the app (for example, by editing the database directly). Check the audit log to see what happened and who did it.
Recalculate accepts the current data as valid: only use it after reviewing, or after a migration or a restore.

preguntas.p: How do I create and restore a backup?
r: The button in the Backup tab saves a copy of every collection on the server. You can also run node scripts/backup.js from the console.
Restoring is done from the console (node scripts/restore.js): it asks for confirmation and recalculates the check digits when it finishes.

tips.racha: Consecutive days, counting from today, in which you saved the checklist and scored some points.
tips.imc: Body mass index: weight divided by height squared. 18.5 to 24.9 is the normal range. It's only a guide.
tips.adherencia: How much of your plan you followed in the last 7 days. The diet counts every day and the routine only on workout days.
tips.checklist: Done is worth 1 point, Partly half and Skipped 0. It's saved once per day and drives your adherence and streak.
tips.cambiarEjercicio: Shows the next alternative the AI suggested. It's only for now: the swap isn't saved to your plan.
tips.usuarios: Every registered account. Deleting one also deletes its plans and check-ins. Administrators can't be deleted from here.
tips.familias: A family groups permissions and can include other families. What a user can do is the sum of their families and individual permissions.
tips.integridad: Detects data changed outside the app by comparing each record's check digit (DVH) and each collection's (DVV).
tips.bitacora: Record of every request to the app and of important events. It doesn't store passwords or emails.
tips.backup: Copy of every collection on the server. Restoring runs from the console and recalculates the check digits.
